classification.difficultyReason: Add triangle and circle-part areas, identifying a semicircle radius from its diameter and using Pythagoras to obtain a sector radius.

content.prompt: Find the area of the following figures. Give your answers in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: An upper semicircle shares its horizontal diameter with the base of a downward triangle. The diameter is labelled 6 cm, its midpoint O is marked, and a right-side vertical dimension gives the triangle height as 5 cm. The dotted lower extension remains red; ordinary boundaries and centre marker use house black.
spec.mathematics: Semicircle diameter 6 cm; triangle base 6 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm.

answer.worked:
The semicircle has radius $6\div2=3\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac12\times6\times5\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=15\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{semicircle}}&=\frac12\times\pi\times3^2\\A_{\text{semicircle}}&=\frac{9\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{figure}}&=15+\frac{9\pi}{2}\\A_{\text{figure}}&=\left(15+\frac{9\pi}{2}\right)\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A sector of a circle, centre $O$, on a right-angled triangle.

spec.description: A right triangle with horizontal 12 cm base and vertical 5 cm left side lies below a sector. Its hypotenuse is the shared radius, with centre O at the lower-right vertex. The other radius is obtained by rotating the shared radius clockwise through 60 degrees. The sector arc joins their endpoints. Ordinary source blue lines and red centre marker use house black.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular triangle legs 5 cm and 12 cm; sector centre O and central angle 60 degrees. The unlabelled radius is not supplied to students.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the calculated radius and areas are withheld.

answer.short:
$\left(30+\dfrac{169\pi}{6}\right)\text{ cm}^2$

Use Pythagoras to find the shared radius, then add the triangle and sector areas.
answer.worked:
The hypotenuse is the sector radius $r$. By Pythagoras’ theorem:

$$\begin{align*}r^2&=5^2+12^2\\r^2&=25+144\\r^2&=169\\r&=13\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac12\times12\times5\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=30\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

The $60^\circ$ sector is $\frac{60}{360}=\frac16$ of a circle.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac16\times\pi\times13^2\\A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac{169\pi}{6}\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{figure}}&=30+\frac{169\pi}{6}\\A_{\text{figure}}&=\left(30+\frac{169\pi}{6}\right)\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
